headline: Profit soars on favorable currency swing as growth cools
summary_short: Revenue rose 8.1% y/y to $7,352M and diluted EPS jumped 130% to $2.53, driven mainly by a swing to FX and derivative gains versus a year-ago loss; Adjusted EPS grew a much slower 15% to $2.54 once those one-offs are excluded.
summary_long: Q2 revenue grew 8.1% y/y to $7,352M on 9% gross bookings growth; operating income rose 11.1% to $2,500M as opex grew a slower 7%. GAAP diluted EPS jumped 130% to $2.53, driven mainly by a $195M FX/derivative gain on Euro debt versus a $961M year-ago loss, plus lower interest expense; Adjusted EPS grew a slower 15% to $2.54 once those items are excluded. The Board declared a $0.42/share Q3 dividend and repurchased $3.7B of stock, deepening the equity deficit to -$10,783M. Long-term debt rose 18.1% q/q on $2,975M of new H1 debt issuance. Q3 guidance: revenue growth 4%-6%, Adjusted EBITDA growth 4%-6%.
confidence_notes: REGENERATED — this summary was force-regenerated per explicit instruction; no prior summary existed on disk for this period, so this is a fresh from-scratch compose, not an edit of an existing file. Source is the Q2 2026 earnings press release (EX-99.1, q2-26bkngearningsrelease.htm) filed as an exhibit to the Aug 4 2026 8-K; scripts/resolve-edgar-exhibit.mjs found no filename matching the 'EX-99*' pattern in the accession folder, but the folder listing's non-cover, non-index candidate (q2-26bkngearningsrelease.htm) was unambiguously the press release and was fetched directly. All KPI values are SEC-filing-sourced GAAP figures (10-Q/8-K), so no cross-basis clearing was needed. Q/q deltas are seasonally distorted for revenue, operating income, and EPS (Q2 is Booking's peak travel season vs Q1's trough), so y/y is used for those rows; long-term debt instead uses q/q because the quarter's own $2,975M H1 debt issuance is the more informative comparison than the smaller y/y change. GAAP diluted EPS y/y growth computes to 130.0% off the shard's stored $1.10 prior-year EPS vs. the release's own stated +131% — a ~1pp difference from the release using an unrounded prior-year EPS internally, not a data error. FY2026 guidance was disclosed only in qualitative bands (e.g. 'High Single Digits', 'Low to Mid-Teens') with no explicit numeric range, so it was not captured; the six Q3 2026 guidance metrics with explicit numeric ranges (room nights, gross bookings, CC gross bookings, revenue, CC revenue, Adjusted EBITDA growth, all 2026-Q3) were identified but NOT persisted to data/events/BKNG_US.json's guidance[] array — no sanctioned script exists for that write (apply-extended-metrics.mjs only writes event.extendedMetrics[]), and per the tooling-gap rule an ad-hoc write was avoided.

drivers.explanation: Gross bookings grew 9% (8% constant currency) on 5% room-night growth and about 2% higher constant-currency ADRs; Booking.com alternative-accommodation room nights rose 4%.
Total operating expenses grew 7%, slower than revenue's 8% growth; adjusted fixed operating expenses rose 6% on higher cloud-computing and software-license costs and adverse FX.

Driven mainly by a $195M FX/derivative gain on Euro-denominated debt versus a $961M year-ago loss, plus lower interest expense from matured convertible notes; Adjusted EPS excludes these and grew only 15%.
Rose largely from $2,975M of new long-term debt proceeds shown on the six-month cash-flow statement; the release does not break out the quarterly issuance separately.
Driven by $7,758M of six-month share repurchases (treasury stock rose to $62,129M from $54,315M) exceeding net income generated, deepening the accumulated deficit.
CEO Glenn Fogel cited resilient underlying travel demand despite geopolitical and macro uncertainty, and raised expected Transformation Program annual run-rate savings to about $650M by end of 2027.
